clue.text: Coca leaf assortment? Collier may take his pick here

definitions.text: Collier may take his pick here

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed selection, so the letters of the two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A miner rummaging through a mix of coca leaves to pick one out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assortment' tells you to rearrange COCALEAF. The second sentence is the definition: a collier's pick is his mining tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal face is the exposed seam where a miner works with his pick.

clue.text: Lang loses heart in Italian tourist centre

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: Cosmo Gordon Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1930s

explanation.surface: Someone called Lang feeling dispirited on holiday in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lang' calls up Archbishop Cosmo Lang; 'loses heart' removes the central S of COSMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Como is a lakeside town in northern Italy popular with visitors.

clue.text: Right in a wrong way? Wrong!

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
set wrong, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A question about doing right in the wrong way, answered with a rebuke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns WAY into AWY; 'in' places R inside it. 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone awry has gone wrong or amiss.

clue.text: King not to succeed without appeal

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to fail is not to succeed
SA (sex appeal) is crossword shorthand for appeal

explanation.surface: A monarch failing for lack of charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking'; SA, for sex appeal, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Faisal was the name of kings of Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Feeling pity for Scrooge having empty apartment in Advent?

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the other word

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
Scrooge is the miser in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

indicators.note: emptied of its inside, leaving only first and last letters

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry for Scrooge alone in an empty flat at Christmas time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips the inside of 'apartment'; Scrooge is the type of the miser, and the Advent season leads to Christmas, when his story is set. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To commiserate is to express sympathy, so commiserating is pitying someone.

clue.text: Listen for an insect

definitions.meaning: as a verb it means to eavesdrop, to listen in secretly
the name of a small insect with pincers at its tail

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to eavesdrop; as a noun it names a pincered insect.

clue.text: Lover of Shakespeare writing here and there, say

parts.note: Mark Antony is Cleopatra's lover in Shakespeare's play
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare fan scribbling notes everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here and there, say' gives an example: the two words are opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Here and there are words of opposite meaning, an example of the term for opposites.

clue.text: Bridge player less than generous with child prodigy

parts.note: West is one of the four players in bridge, abbreviated W
under means less than
kind means generous

explanation.surface: A stingy bridge partner who plays alongside a gifted child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wunderkind (German for wonder child) is a prodigy who succeeds young.

clue.text: Chasm may be providing income for landowner

definitions.meaning: a chasm is a split or tear in the earth
rent paid to a freeholder for the land a building stands on

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, a chasm is a rent (tear) in the ground; 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In British leasehold, this is the regular payment a leaseholder makes to the freeholder of the land.

clue.text: Mother stuffing birds on November 11

indicators.note: one piece stuffing another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: martins are birds of the swallow family
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum cramming birds with stuffing for a feast on 11 November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; the date itself is the definition, St Martin's day.
explanation.definitionFit: The feast of St Martin falls on 11 November, a traditional date for eating goose.

clue.text: Doubtless, mistake offends client

indicators.note: read as mis-take, taking the letters wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A blunder that offends a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' signals the rearrangement of OFFENDS CLIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure of oneself means having no doubt.

clue.text: In Kensington, dozens joined art circle

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A gathering of dozens of artists in a fashionable London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals letters found inside: KensingTON DOzens. 'joined' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tondo is a circular painting or relief, a round artwork.

clue.text: Old entertainer responsible for trick of the light?

definitions.text: Old entertainer responsible for trick of the light?

parts.words: Old entertainer responsible for trick of the light?
parts.note: a bygone device for entertainment whose shows were illusions made by projecting light, playing on a conjurer's trick

explanation.definitionFit: A Victorian projector of painted slides, an early form of entertainment by light.

clue.text: Retreat? Nevertheless, pull in

indicators.note: the second piece is put inside the first

parts.note: withal is an old word for nevertheless
to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A general weighing whether to retreat yet still pull his troops in.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the noun sense of the definition, a retreat by an army.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawal is a pulling back, a military retreat.

clue.text: Turn back before getting renewed energy

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
to wind is to turn, as a handle

explanation.surface: An athlete turns back, then gets a fresh burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' as a verb, to support a motion; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is a fresh surge of stamina after tiring.

clue.text: Killing time in Rome (ie wasting time)

definitions.text: Killing time in Rome (ie wasting time)

parts.words: Killing time in Rome (ie wasting time)
parts.note: a Roman calendar date remembered for an assassination, with the bracket teasing that killing time normally means idling

explanation.walkthrough: Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March; the bracket pretends 'killing time' is only the idiom for idling.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was stabbed on the Ides of March, so this Roman date was a time of killing.

clue.text: One blessed with implant, imbued with energy

indicators.note: something imbued with a quality has it soaked into it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a pacemaker is a device implanted to regulate the heartbeat
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A heart patient, blessed with a pacemaker, feels newly energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside PACEMAKER after the P. 'One blessed' recalls the Beatitudes: 'Blessed are the peacemakers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sermon on the Mount names those who make peace among the blessed.

clue.text: Article by northeast writer taking drink to drown sorrows

indicators.note: means next to, setting the pieces side by side

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A northern writer drinking to forget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepenthe is a drug in Homer said to banish grief, a potion of forgetfulness.

clue.text: Nose being cut off by nurse provides entertainment

indicators.note: having its end cut off, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: hooter is British slang for the nose
a nanny is a children's nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse slicing off a patient's nose, which somehow entertains onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut off' trims the R from HOOTER, leaving HOOTE; 'by' puts NANNY beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hootenanny is an informal folk-music party, a kind of lively entertainment.

clue.text: Clergyman not starting immediately

indicators.note: the word loses the letter it starts with

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral

explanation.surface: A churchman reluctant to get going straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops the C from CANON.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for at once, soon, straightaway.

clue.text: 50% of dumb animals needed money

indicators.note: half of the word, here its first two letters

parts.note: cats are animals

explanation.surface: Half-witted animals in need of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' takes DU, the first half of 'dumb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducats were gold coins once used across Europe.

clue.text: Apple pie I could desire

indicators.note: printer's pie is type spilt into a jumble, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a slice of apple pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple pie' looks like one dish; 'pie' (printer's jumbled type) is the anagram signal for I COULD DESIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Delicious is a well-known American variety of eating apple.

clue.text: Musical performance — Toscanini's last

parts.note: a gig is a performance

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A conductor's final concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' is a noun, the stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe musical, a stage show and film.

clue.text: Composer missing a little grebe from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, read from the bottom upwards, so backwards
a little is cut off the end, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A composer who has lost sight of a small water bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing a little' trims GREBE to GREB; 'from the south' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Hold back to hold front of seat belt here?

indicators.note: one piece holding another contains it

parts.note: to wait is to hold back

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An instruction on fastening a seat belt before a car moves off.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the front of 'seat', goes inside WAIT. 'belt here?' defines by example: a belt is worn here.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is fastened round the middle of the body, at the narrowing below the ribs.

clue.text: Anger management? Eat and drink!

indicators.note: managing letters means handling and rearranging them

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Advice for anger management: eat and drink to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as advice to calm down with food; 'management' is really the signal to rearrange the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet pomegranate syrup used in drinks and cocktails.

clue.text: Run from large snake

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large in clothing sizes
an adder is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing from a big snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is not a verb here: it is a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in stockings or tights is also called a ladder in British usage.

clue.text: Hoarding shows popular musician hugging tree

indicators.note: one piece hugging another wraps round it

parts.note: Sting is the stage name of a famous pop singer
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A billboard showing a pop star embracing a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoarding' looks like a billboard, but it is the verb: keeping a store. 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashing away goods is storing them secretly, the same as hoarding.
